gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-toto: Grandstander's lines never swell or thin, and its letters stay open. Grandstander is the one that shouts with confidence, while Noto Serif Toto does the dignified work, its heavy chalk-like lowercase shifting only mildly in stroke weight.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-vithku: Expressive is the right word for Grandstander, whose marker-nib line ignores direction and keeps its letters open. But Noto Serif Vithkuqi brings gentle weight variation and big round bowls, which gives the text serif an editorial feel.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-serif-yezidi: Grandstander draws downstrokes and connecting curves with no shift in weight, which keeps its bold letters open and direct. Noto Serif Yezidi is the sturdy half, its joins slimming noticeably while words still come across as solid blocks.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-odor-mean-chey: Grandstander leads with open, bold letters whose curves carry as much weight as its straight stems. Odor Mean Chey pinches its a, s and e nearly shut, and that open-against-closed tension is what this pairing does best.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-pt-serif-caption: PT Serif Caption reads tall and literary, with a visibly large x-height. Grandstander is the bold, expressive one with crossbars matching its stems, while the text serif only hints at modulation when you look closely.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-suez-one: Suez One reads bookish and refined, its tall-bowled e and a reached only through a thin channel into each counter. Grandstander bends bold, constant-width wire; the serif keeps things refined.
gen-gf-grandstander-lora: Grandstander's marker-like lines hold a constant width, with short ascenders and a tall x-height that make it bold and expressive. Lora is the literary one, with a broad c and modest hairlines.
gen-gf-grandstander-merriweather: Cozy and a little stocky, the body sits under Grandstander's bold heading with a tall middle band and soft stroke contrast. Merriweather would settle into a refined rhythm across paragraphs, each curve hinting at wedge-shaped pen pressure.
gen-gf-grenze-gf-cascadia-code: Grenze cuts its letters like stencils, with mildly varied bar widths, barely-there ascenders and tight spacing that feel literary. Cascadia Code then runs in a wire-thin line, spaced wide enough to glide.
gen-gf-grenze-gf-julius-sans-one: Julius Sans One reads clean and approachable, with wide stretches of blank space between letters and capitals barely taller than lowercase. But Grenze's tightly fitted, gently tapering letters supply the literary side.
